fix(formatter): decide JSX opening element layout from collapsed Tailwind class string
prs.author: jaehafe
prs.body:
## Summary With `sortTailwindcss` enabled (and `preserveWhitespace` off), formatting a JSX element whose Tailwind class string spans multiple lines is not idempotent. It takes two runs to reach a stable output. Input (`{"sortTailwindcss": {}}`): ```tsx const A = (
Hello
); ``` 1st run: ```tsx const A = (
Hello
); ``` 2nd run: ```tsx const A =
Hello
; ``` ### Cause `FormatOpeningElement` decides its layout from the attribute's **source** string value: - `SingleStringAttribute` is used only if the value has no line break. - Otherwise the attributes group is forced to expand if any string value has a line break. But for a Tailwind attribute without `preserveWhitespace`, `write_tailwind_string_literal` collapses all whitespace (including line breaks) into single spaces. So the printed value has no line break while the layout was decided as if it had one. The next run sees a single-line value and joins the element. prettier-plugin-tailwindcss rewrites the attribute value in the AST before printing, so Prettier makes the layout decision on the collapsed value and gets the 2nd-run output in one pass. ### Fix Decide the layout from whether the **printed** value has a line break. A Tailwind attribute (per `is_tailwind_jsx_attribute`) with `preserveWhitespace` off is treated as single-line. Nothing changes when `sortTailwindcss` is off, wi …(truncated)

prs.title: fix(formatter): decide template and object key layouts from collapsed Tailwind classes
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Follow-up to #28744, same root cause in other places.

With `sortTailwindcss` on and `preserveWhitespace` off, Tailwind class strings and templates are printed with their whitespace collapsed, but these layout decisions read the source text, so formatting took two runs:

```ts
// Sole template argument of a Tailwind call
const a = clsx(`
  p-4 flex items-center ${active ? "bg-white" : "bg-black"} text-black
`);
// Arrow body tagged with a Tailwind function
const b = () => tw`
  p-4 flex items-center bg-white text-black
`;
// Short object key (tabWidth: 4)
const c = clsx({ "a   b": someLongCondition });
```

- `is_multiline_template_starting_on_same_line` now returns `false` for a template whose line breaks are collapsed
  - It reads the current Tailwind context (what `TemplateElement` reads) or the one a Tailwind tag pushes, so the arrow body, sole argument and member chain routing callers follow the print
- `write_tailwind_string_literal` returns its printed width, and `write_member_name` uses it for the short key decision
  - An upper bound: the sorter also drops duplicates of known classes
- `tailwind_context_for_callee` is shared by the call and tagged template pushes and the layout check, like `tailwind_context_for_jsx_attribute` in #28744

Outputs match Prettier + prettier-plugin-tailwindcss and are idempotent.

Not covered here: `is_short_argument` (#28745), Tailwind calls through `MemberChain` never pushing the context, and computed keys.

AI assistance (Claude Code)

prs.title: fix(transformer/class-properties): preserve private method values in assignments
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
Compound assignments and updates to private methods call the method body while reading its value. For example, `this.#method ||= rhs()` calls `#method`, evaluates `rhs()` when the method returns `undefined`, and throws instead of returning the method function.

Distinguish method reads from accessor getter calls when lowering assignments and updates. Method reads now return the function through the existing brand check. Regression coverage includes static and instance methods, all compound operators, prefix/postfix updates, failed brand checks, and receivers obtained from function calls.

Validation:

- 39 Rust unit/integration tests and 53 Node binding tests passed.
- Clippy and Rust formatting checks passed.
- Transform conformance adds one passing output fixture and one passing executable fixture; existing failures are unchanged.
- Transformer coverage has no new failures against Test262, Babel, TypeScript, and local cases.
- Cross-target probes passed at ES2021, ES2020, and ES2015.

AI assistance was used to implement and test this change.

prs.author: jaehafe

## Summary

Follow-up to #28744, same kind of issue in a different place.

With `sortTailwindcss` enabled, an assignment whose right side is a Tailwind function call can take two runs to reach a stable output, because the "short argument" check measures the argument's **source** text while the printed text has its whitespace collapsed.

Input (`{"sortTailwindcss": {"functions": ["cn"]}}`, default `printWidth: 100`):

```ts

);
```

```ts

  cn("flex p-4");
```

When the argument is sorted as Tailwind classes, whitespace is collapsed when printed, so the source can be "long" while the printed text is "short". Prettier sees the already rewritten value, so it decides on the printed text.

fix(codegen): print infinite numeric literals as `1e400` instead of `Infinity`
prs.author: d3lm
prs.body:
Without `minify`, codegen prints an infinite `NumericLiteral` as the identifier `Infinity`. `Infinity` is a global property, not a literal, so a local binding can shadow it:

```js
function f(Infinity) { return 1e400; }
// before: `return Infinity;`, so `f(5)` returns `5`
// after:  `return 1e400;`,    so `f(5)` returns `Infinity`
```

- Without `minify`, infinite literals now print as `1e400` (and `-1e400`)
  - `1e400` has an exponent, so member access (`1e400.toString`) and keyword spacing need no special handling
- With `minify`, the output stays `1/0`. It was already shadow-safe, so minified size does not change (`minsize.snap` unchanged)
- Removed the `delete (0, Infinity)` workaround in `UnaryExpression`, since `delete 1e400` is valid in strict mode
- Minifier tests print their output without `minify`, so 37 expectations for folded infinite literals now read `1e400` instead of `Infinity`. Inputs and the tests where `Infinity` is a real identifier are unchanged

Not covered here:

- Infinite method keys that are not computed, such as `({ 1e400() {} })` and `class { 1e400() {} }`, still minify to invalid `1/0(){}`. This existed before and needs changes in several key-printing paths
- A few minifier paths create `NaN`/`Infinity` literals without checking for shadowing (e.g. `function f(NaN) { return Number.NaN }`)
- Enum lowering in the transformer and in isolated declarations still emits `Infinity` identifiers

prs.title: fix(minifier): preserve UTF-16 boundaries in empty-search replaceAll folding
prs.author: huuyafwww
prs.body:
Hi, I found this while checking a tsdown/Rolldown update.
Folding `replaceAll` with an empty search string currently inserts the replacement between Unicode scalar values, but JavaScript inserts it between UTF-16 code units.
For example:

```js
export default () => ((replacement) => "a😀z".replaceAll("", replacement))("-");
```

The original returns `"-a-\ud83d-\ude00-z-"`, while main folds it to `"-a-😀-z-"`.
The IIFE parameter propagation exposes the same problem as a direct literal call.

The fix uses the existing `JSStrBuilder` to append each UTF-16 code unit and its replacement.
The result reserves its exact WTF-8 byte length once, with checked capacity arithmetic, and an empty replacement returns the original string.
`replace`, nonempty searches, and the existing side-effect, substitution-pattern, and lone-surrogate input guards keep their current paths.

The regression test covers supplementary characters, adjacent surrogate pairs, a supplementary replacement, empty receiver/replacement, and the IIFE case above.
It fails on main and passes with the fix.
On macOS arm64 with Rust 1.99.1 and Node 24.22.1, the `oxc_ecmascript` and `oxc_minifier` suites pass (786 tests; 26 existing ignored tests), as does Clippy for both crates.
I also built the five compiler NAPI packages: their suites pass with 1,212 tests, 14 skipped tests, and 1 todo.
The E2E suite passes all 313 tests.
`cargo minsize`, `cargo allocs`, and minifier conformance leave the checked-in snapshots unchanged; t
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(lexer): count LS, PS and non-ASCII whitespace in comment newline flags
prs.author: vshalpnjabi
prs.body:
Fixes #28318

The comment newline flags only looked at ASCII whitespace and `\n`/`\r`. A U+2028/U+2029 line terminator, or non-ASCII whitespace such as U+00A0 between the comment and the line break, was missed, so the flags came out wrong.

This adds small scalar helpers in `carve/comments.rs` that step over Unicode whitespace and treat LS and PS as line terminators, in both directions. No AVX2 path is touched.

Testing:
- New `crates/oxc_lexer/tests/comment_newlines.rs` covers the cases from the issue plus ASCII controls. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.
- `cargo test -p oxc_lexer --all-features` and `cargo test -p oxc_parser` pass.
- `cargo clippy -p oxc_lexer --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
- Lexer coverage snapshots updated: one more Babel and one more Test262 case now pass (`single-line-html-close-unicode-separators`).
- This touches a different part of `comments.rs` than #28536 (for #28317). I checked that the two merge cleanly apart from the snapshot counts, and the lexer tests pass with both applied.

AI-assisted; I reviewed the full diff and ran the tests myself.

fix(linter/vitest/prefer-called-exactly-once-with): avoid panic on non-ASCII text
prs.author: magurotuna
prs.body:
Fixes #28849

`get_source_code_line_span` sliced the source text at every byte offset back to the line start, and at `statement_span.end + 1`. If a multi-byte character was in either place, the rule panicked, also without `--fix`.

This PR finds the line start with `rfind('\n')`, and extends the end by the `len_utf8()` of the next char. For ASCII text, the span does not change.

Added two fail cases and two fix cases. Each case panics without this change.

I used AI assistance (Claude Code) to write this change. I reviewed the code and ran the tests.

fix(codegen): keep one source map mapping per generated position
prs.author: magurotuna
prs.body:
Fixes #28843

### Summary

Some printed tokens map to removed text, for example `verify` in `public verify() {}` maps to `public`. See the issue for details.

### Fix

`SourcemapBuilder::add_source_mapping` skipped a new mapping only if it had the same original position as the last one. Now, if a new mapping has the same generated position as the last token, it replaces the last token. Nothing was printed between the two mappings, so the new mapping is for the printed token.

TypeScript's source map generator also overwrites a pending mapping at the same generated position, unless the original position moves backward ([`addMapping` in TypeScript 7](tsc/internal/sourcemap/generator.go#L237-L258)).

`packages/codegen/src-js/print/write.ts` gets the same rule.

Three existing unit tests in `sourcemap_builder.rs` passed the full output to both calls, so both mappings had the same generated position. Codegen does not do this: it passes the output that is printed so far. I changed the tests to do the same as codegen. The assertions do not change.

On 3,508 TypeScript files from 251 npm packages, `oxc-transform` 0.157.0 gives duplicate mappings in 690 files. With this change, no file has them.

I wrote this change with AI assistance (Claude Code). I reviewed the code and ran the tests.

prs.body: `react/only-export-components` treated JSX values as components and reported unrelated utility exports. Classify JSX elements and fragments as non-component exports, including named exports, to match `eslint-plugin-react-refresh@0.5.7`. ```tsx export const CLOSED_ICON = closed; export const STATUS_LABELS = { open: 'Open', closed: 'Closed' }; ``` This module now passes.
